title: Corner-coverage measurement matrix on the accepted S11 tree (pure measurement, zero product changes)
motivation: The S11 closure (commit d6ecea11) measured only the 24-step, 1024^2, cold, 12x2 corner (chain 1452.5935 s). The campaign success criteria require measured per-corner timings across small/large tiles, 1/24/72+ timesteps, cold/warm runs, and serial/parallel workloads. This protocol freezes those corners BEFORE any timing, per the Phase-0 discipline (pre-register protocols, then measure).

tree_pin.note: Post-hardening tree (supersedes 75e03c62... for future runs per the S11 closure). The E2E-measured 12x2 configuration prices byte-identically under this tree (2,908,028,928 B/job; batteries byte-identical to the accepted state). Every job asserts this pin at start and aborts on drift. Pin semantics: head_commit must be an ANCESTOR of the running HEAD and the src/pyproject diff vs base_commit must match expected_product_diff_files + sha256 exactly (docs/evidence-only commits after the pin are permissible).

variant_construction.steps_2: header + first 2 data rows of the corpus metfile (hours 0,1 of id 200)
variant_construction.steps_72: header + 3 day-blocks of 24 hourly rows (id 200/201/202); columns other than id byte-identical to the day-200 rows; both dated and undated filenames written per tile as the corpus does
variant_construction.small_256: gdal.Translate srcWin [0,0,256,256] of every tile raster in Building_DSM/Trees/DEM into a fresh 24-tile scene; metfiles copied; variant manifest with sha256s recorded
variant_construction.large_2048: phase2/b0_generate_corpus_2048.py (deterministic single-tile 2048^2 generator, reused from Stage-B0 job 14100529) into a fresh scene; manifest sha recorded

large-tile corner at the production-viable shape (AMENDMENT 2026-10-16, pre-timing: c2048p measured a PRE-EXISTING public-API defect instead of a timing -- plan_phase_admission(policy='reject') refuses any phase whose job count is below the requested worker width (runtime_memory.py requested>admissible check; api.py passes the unclamped width), so a 1-tile scene refuses at workers>=2 with a misleading 'only 1 fit' message despite ~4x memory slack; reproduced on login against the pinned tree AND confirmed present on main (runtime_memory.py:948, api.py:235). Defect documented, NOT fixed here (public-behavior change). c2048s measures the corner the way production accepts it: workers=1).
serial corner at the production scale; single worker owning the whole node (the practitioner's serial run); degree-1 export + degree-1 scheduling

corner_contract_notes: 1-step corner is contract-unsupported: pipeline.py raises 'Own-met input must contain multiple rows' for a 1-row metfile (np.loadtxt yields 1-D); the public minimum is 2 rows. Corner c2p measures that minimum; the 1-step refusal is documented, not forced.

The serial corner is workers=1, threads_per_worker=24: one worker owns the node. The 1-thread engine extremity is already covered by the A2/R11 paired probes (engine 1x2=347.9 s, 1x3=301.7 s, 8t=264 s, TMRT bitwise in all arms); repeating it at chain scale would add ~7 h of node time for a thread-scaling fact already measured.

SVF artifacts are timestep-independent, so every 1024^2 24-tile arm (c24p, c24w, c2p, c72p, c24s) gates SVF bitwise against the frozen corpus goldens; TMRT gates apply only where the step count matches the golden (24 steps).

No external goldens exist for 2/72-step TMRT, the 256^2 crop, or 2048^2: those arms record band counts (== met rows), all-finite checks, and artifact sha256s. Large-tile cross-thread numerical equality is already pinned by Stage-B0 (2048^2 TMRT bitwise 24/24 across 1x8/1x2, job 14100529). The c256p/c256s pair gates SVF+TMRT bitwise EQUAL between the two configs (cross-config determinism at the small corner).

numerical.c24p: SVF bitwise 24/24 vs phase0/p1c_svf_base38 AND TMRT 24/24 bands vs phase0/p2_ref_TMRT.tif
numerical.c24s: same as c24p (serial machinery bitwise at production scale)
numerical.c2p: SVF bitwise 24/24 vs p1c_svf_base38; TMRT band count == 2; all-finite
numerical.c72p: SVF bitwise 24/24 vs p1c_svf_base38; TMRT band count == 72; all-finite
numerical.c256p: TMRT band count == 24; SVF+TMRT all-finite; shas recorded
numerical.c256s: SVF + TMRT bitwise EQUAL to c256p for all 24 tiles
numerical.c2048p: TMRT band count == 24; SVF+TMRT all-finite; shas recorded; OR the documented admission-refusal record (defect discovery)
numerical.c2048s: TMRT band count == 24; SVF+TMRT all-finite; shas recorded

gates.admission: every arm records the plan_phase_admission echo (admissible_workers, per-job price, base, budget) under its own runtime options; c24/c256 arms must admit (12-wide is the accepted state at 1024^2; trivial at 256^2); c2048p primary 4x6 expected to admit 4 (4 x ~11.6 GB <= base); a refusal of the primary is recorded and the pre-declared fallback shape runs
gates.chain_band: c24p chain within [1380, 1525] s (+-5% of the E2E anchor 1452.5935) as a cross-tree sanity band; informational for all other arms
gates.attribution: per-arm phase split walls / svf (barrier + export stage, barrier timed parent-side around execute_geometry_phase) / run, plus runtime env echo

run_policy: ONE timed pass per arm; zero retries except a single causal retry on a documented infrastructure anomaly (exercised once: jobs 14107911/14107913 died in the UNTIMED prime -- three concurrent jobs raced on the hardcoded shared phase0/scene_64 probe scene; no timed work lost; retry used a job-private prime scene). Jobs C1 (c24p,c24w,c2p,c72p), C2 (c256p,c256s,c2048p), C3 (c24s) are independent Slurm jobs (24 CPU, 96G each) and may run concurrently on different nodes. Job C4 (c2048s) was added by the pre-timing amendment above after C2 recorded the c2048p admission defect. Variant/scene construction and the numba prime are untimed.
efficiency_deliverable: corner_matrix_findings.json: per-corner chain + phase table; serial/parallel ratios (c24s vs c24p, c256s vs c256p); warm/cold deltas (c24w vs c24p); timestep scaling of the run phase (2/24/72); tile-size scaling (256^2/1024^2/2048^2); updated remaining-headroom statement feeding the barrier-seam (X04) feasibility read from measured barrier/export/run attribution across shapes.
review_status: No product change is involved in this phase (pure measurement on the accepted, already-reviewed tree); the pre-E2E independent-review rule for accepted numerical/scheduling changes does not trigger here. A barrier-seam CHANGE candidate (X04) arising from these measurements would follow the full protocol -> implementation -> independent review -> E2E arc before acceptance.
actual_target_status: unverified (synthetic corpus only, as throughout the campaign)
